quest.title: Into the Woods
quest.description: You and Paimon put in a good amount of hard work to sort your stories into a version that the children might find interesting. Thankfully, they like your stories. Although they don't seem to have told the truth about the mysterious creatures, this isn't the time to go into detail. Now, go with Rana to clear out some Withering Zones. You're doing this so the children of Vimara Village can play safely, after all.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

talks.objective: Go to the Withering Zone that needs to be cleaned up
Go to the Withering Zone that needs to be cleaned up

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Whew, it's nice to have the chance to do something. This should help with our problem a little.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Besides, watching you fight made me realize that I still have a lot to learn, {NICKNAME}! Like footwork... and timing too...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: An experienced traveler like you is just... absolutely amazing!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #Thank you so much, really. That reminds me, how's your condition, {NICKNAME}? After taking care of so many Withering Zones, do you feel dizzy or nauseous or anything?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: That's good... You've done so much. Goodness, I feel so much better now.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Let's take a break! One of our forest patrol campsites isn't far from here. It should have equipment and supplies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Camping! That sounds fun!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Then off we go! It's just ahead.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Eh? I—I see, lie down, quickly! I'll go get help...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hey! Don't make jokes like that, {NICKNAME}! You'll worry Rana.

choices.text: Paimon has me on a strict training regimen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Heh, well, we're always improving together as companions!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Here we are. When I was little, I would often take this road to go down to the river valley to play.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: The Withering Zones are appearing so quickly now, and Tighnari and the others are too busy to deal with them in time. But it's a good thing we have you here now.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Leave it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Okay! You made clean work of those Withering Zones before, but they're still dangerous. If it gets to be too much, be sure to leave the realm and take some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Here we are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's that round thing at the edge, the thing that looks like a small cabin?

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Oh, that... I'm not sure where it came from, but you see them all the time in the forests of Sumeru. Maybe it's some kind of ruin!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Strange, since you've asked, I seem to have heard about this kind of house and its resident. Who was it again... It wasn't that researcher who's in Satyavada Life...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Oh, never mind! {NICKNAME}, Paimon, wait here for a second! I'm gonna go tidy up the campsite, get a fire going, and get some ingredients ready!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let us help you!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I can't have that! I was the one who asked you to come and help clean up the Withering Zones...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just think of us as trainee Forest Watchers! What do you need us to do, Rana?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Well, if you insist, Paimon... Hmm... Could you help me get some firewood then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #All you need is some wood chopped? That's nothing, {NICKNAME} could do that.

choices.text: No, we'll need to collect some dried branches...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #That's right, you know your stuff, {NICKNAME}! You'd make a fine Forest Watcher!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Is that so? Hm... Okay, got it. Let's go, {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: I am pretty great at chopping wood.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Ah, you won't need to do that. You'll just need to pick up some dried branches off the ground. Collecting firewood is one of the fundamentals of wilderness survival!

talks.objective: Go to the Withering Zone that needs to be cleaned up

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: You guys are back! I'm almost done here as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Will these be enough, Rana?

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Yep, that's more than enough!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Oh, right! One of our camping traditions is to have the most esteemed person in the group light the campfire.

choices.text: They just have to light it, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Leave it to us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really, quit fooling around! Don't act like we haven't burned anything along our journey...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: This Withering Zone's expanding...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Regardless, I'll leave it in your capable hands just like before, {NICKNAME}. Just don't overdo it...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #Thanks, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Using the supplies stored at the campsite and the ingredients gathered along the way, Rana makes a pot of richly fragrant curry.\nEveryone stuffs their faces.\nThe rest is packed up in containers for later use.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: ...Ahh! It's so good. Curry tastes even better after hard work.

choices.text: Sounds like Rana stole Paimon's line.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't care about such things!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Still, this curry is so aromatic. What if the smell draws some critters or hilichurls over here?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: "Curry, curry, in the air~ Hungry children it's time to come home~♪"

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: This is a children's song from Sumeru. There's something free about curry — each family adds different ingredients and spices depending on how they make it. So, each family's curry has its own flavor.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: So, when we were little, we could smell a curry and tell whether it was made by our parents.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: But once we got older, we couldn't tell whose curry was whose anymore. They all seem about the same.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: But still, you know that it's time to go home and eat when you smell curry!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Curry, curry, in the air~♪"

choices.text: "Hungry children it's time to come home~♪"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #The stuff you make also has a different aroma, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Oh? Is that so? I'd like to try!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But we've just eaten so much of this curry. Let's make something next time!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Okay...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That reminds Paimon, why do you have to pick up branches instead of chopping down trees when you want to start a fire? Does the Dendro Archon punish people who cut down trees? Wah... {NICKNAME}, what do we do!?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Oh, no! It's because fresh wood has too much moisture in it, so it's hard to light. Also, the Dendro Archon isn't that petty!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Still, our teachings in Sumeru also say to respect nature and the forest, because we are the forest's subjects. So are the birds and beasts, and...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: In the end, the forest will remember.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: "...Even if you grow up and forget, don't fret. The forest will remember."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh... Rana, what's wrong?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Eh? Oh... I felt like I almost remembered something that was lost in my memories for a long time. Something warm and precious, but I couldn't remember it all... Just those two lines...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Dang it, it's like when you have to sneeze, but it just won't come out. How infuriating!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Some things are harder to remember the more you try to remember them!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Just ignore it, and after a while, it might suddenly come back to you when you're doing something else!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I'll try. Thanks again for watching those kids in the village for me before. They're like my little brothers and sisters.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: The oldest one is Kavus. He wants to travel the world by boat when he grows up. Sudabeh is his little sister, she says she wants to be just like me. It's a little embarrassing, hehe.

choices.text: I don't think there's anything embarrassing about that.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Then there's Iotham. I'm more worried about him. He was raised by Granny Jehiet after being abandoned in the village.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? So Iotham was...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Yes. I was still just a little girl back then. One day, the adults discovered that a traveling couple who'd been staying in the village were gone. All they left behind was this teeny tiny child.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: I always used to worry about him. But now, he and Kavus and the others are like a family. Alphonso also looks after him, just like a real older brother would.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About what you and the children were talking about before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, now that you mention it, when we were telling stories to the children, we also asked around...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Ah, that's the round, plantlike little fairies you mentioned before...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... They said they didn't know, but they were acting like they were hiding something about the "Aranara."

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Hmm... I don't know much about these creatures myself, but I'll tell you the part I heard. First of all, they're much like you described: round and plantlike.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: The forest is vast and deep here in Sumeru, and it's constantly changing, like a gargantuan beast. So, even locals will lose their way, let alone travelers.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Legend has it that there are countless bizarre and amazing creatures in forests like this, and the most famous among them are the Aranara, which, supposedly, means the "forest people."

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: The Aranara are related to the Dendro Archon and are the guardians of the forest. They're the bridge between people and trees. They also have the ability to enter dreams.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: ...But for the people of Sumeru, dreams are very rare.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That sounds amazing!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Agreed. They might not say it in front of the adults, but I think they really like the legend of the Aranara. Who knows, maybe they've seen an Aranara while playing in the forest.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: It's normal for children to have secrets amongst themselves that they keep from grown-ups. So long as they can grow up healthy, and become strong, kind, and good adults...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Also, about kids going missing...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Ah, about that... Eh? Do you have any clues?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We were also really worried, so we asked around! The kids said that they were in the woods, and the next thing they knew, they were in Vimara Village. They couldn't remember anything that had happened before that.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: That's right. Kavus and Sudabeh suddenly appeared in the village after going missing for a few days. Everyone was worried sick while they were gone, Alphonso even organized a search and rescue team...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: *chuckle*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What is it, Rana?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Now that I think about it, it was actually kinda funny. Remember what I said about curry before? Alphonso made the search party take curry into the forest with them so the children could smell it.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Anyway, we didn't find Kavus or Sudabeh, but they came home on their own. And with the whole memory loss situation... something about this whole thing just doesn't feel right...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: So, I've been patrolling the forest and ruling out any elements that could harm the children. Iotham is the only one left who hasn't gone missing, so I have to protect him.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: About Alphonso...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, speaking of him... Alphonso seems like he's really popular in Vimara Village! He organized the search party, and the kids talk about him all the time...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Oh, him? He's like an older brother to them. We've treated him like family since he arrived in the village a few years ago.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: According to him, like Iotham, he doesn't have any family, so he sees this place as his real home. Iotham also sees him as his actual big brother.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #If you two stayed in Vimara Village, I know they'd be very happy to have another {M#big brother and big sister}{F#two big sisters}!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Like I said before, if it's possible, I hope that you can join the ranks of the Watchers. And we will patrol together. What do you think?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, I'm actually traveling to find someone...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You briefly explain the reason for your travels to Rana.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #I see. I understand how you feel, {NICKNAME}. I also had a friend who was very dear to me vanish out of nowhere. But they...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #Well, that's not important. The {M#blonde girl}{F#blond boy} you're looking for... I feel like I've heard about {M#her}{F#him} somewhere before. Let me think...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #...Nope, I can't remember. I'm sure someone told me a story about a {M#blonde girl}{F#blond boy} before... Just like gold... and called a "Nara" or something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Paimon feels like Rana's memory isn't too good.)

choices.text: (That's what happens when you grow up.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no need to force yourself, Rana. Paimon hopes the kids in Vimara Village are doing okay...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Well, I'm very happy that I could meet the two of you. I'm sure the children feel the same way!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: You're not only skilled but also so kind, and I'm so moved that you would worry about my little brothers and sisters in Vimara Village! I'll keep an eye out for the person you're looking for!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Then, when you finish your journey, come to Sumeru! We can patrol the forest together!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Okay, but think about it. If only I could have met you and Paimon earlier...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Tee-hee, you are making Paimon blush!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Zzz...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (She can even sleep while sitting upright! Is this some special training Forest Watchers get?)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #(She must be exhausted. Hehe, looks like Rana doesn't have our stamina. Do you want to take a rest, {NICKNAME}?)

choices.text: (Yeah, I'm gonna have a little nap, too.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Sleep well!)

choices.text: (There's still something I need to do.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Okay. If you want to rest, just come on back.)

choices.text: (She can sleep even while sitting upright!)

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Ah, about that... Eh? Do you have any clues?

response.speaker: Paimon

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Eh? Why...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh, {NICKNAME} means that we just ate so much of this curry, so maybe another time!

choices.text: It doesn't have to be curry to make Paimon drool.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Humph, looks like you haven't noticed, {NICKNAME}, but the food you make just smells different!

talks.objective: Go to the area where the Spinocrocodiles are active

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Forest Watchers are also tasked with protecting the ecosystem. Recently, potentially because of the Withering Zones, the alligators have become... shall we say, unusually manic.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Not only have they been invading other animals' territories, but they're reproducing at a faster rate. If this goes on, they won't just be a danger to the children, but to the forest's ecosystem as well.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Luckily, your opponent isn't a Withering Zone this time. It's my time to shine, hehe. You rest up, {NICKNAME}, leave this one to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're coming to help too!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Is it really okay...? That's great then, I'll finally get to fight side by side with you!

talks.objective: Defeat a certain number of Spinocrocodiles

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: One of our camping traditions is to have the most esteemed person in the group light the campfire.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Why the tradition? Probably because in the era of darkness, fire was a symbol of warmth and courage.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The era of darkness?

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Right. The origins of the Forest Rangers go way back. The earliest rangers were the forest king's royal guards! I heard that they once walked in forests where there were real tigers.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Later, Khaenri'ah fell, and thus began the era of darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: But not many documents have survived the cataclysm, so no one really knows what exactly happened. Still, I want to see a real tiger!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Ahh... I slept so well! I don't even remember falling asleep, sorry about that, hehe...

choices.text: You can sleep even while sitting upright...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Not really, I just ate a lot and was feeling so relaxed that I just...

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Ahem! Here's a little Forest Watcher trivia for you: When searching for a missing person in the forest, you want to feed them something that's easy to digest when you find them.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Digestion consumes stamina. That's why you feel sleepy easily after eating. Or at least, that's what the Akademiya researchers say.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, have you rested? You worked so hard yesterday...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Don't worry about us!

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Are you sure? Okay then... Thank you so much for yesterday. I feel much better now that you're here.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Heh, you can count on {NICKNAME}! Is there any work left to do today, Rana?

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Let me see... I think we're just about done here. Let's head back to Vimara Village! We can check in on the situation on our way back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, let's go!

choices.text: You must have been exhausted before...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup, that should be enough!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go find Rana!

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: It's good to have you here. But still, don't push yourself.

talks.objective: Return to the camp and talk to Rana

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, you're back! I was so worried...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: I was afraid you and Paimon had run off... or worse, that those alligators from before came back for revenge and hauled you both away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are alligators really that scary!? We saw that you were sleeping, so we went to take care of some other things...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Sorry, I didn't even realize that I had fallen asleep, hehe...

choices.text: You can sleep even while sitting upright...

response.speaker: Rana

response.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: #Besides firewood, we have sufficient supplies of everything else here... Ah, {NICKNAME}, you're back! Have you collected enough firewood?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not yet...

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: It's fine, leave it to me. Just stay here and rest up! Let me just clean up here and I'll go right away!

choices.text: Let me do it. It won't take long.

response.speaker: Rana
response.text: Alright. Thanks.

choices.text: I just wanted to tell you that I'm going now.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Withering Zones are dangerous. If it gets to be too much for you, be sure to leave and take some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Rana
dialogues.text: Zzz... Help find them... Curry...

choices.text: (I should take a little nap as well.)
(I'd better find something else to do for now.)
